tasks.short: Provide formal and informal education to other staff members.

steps.what: Prepare notes to provide formal education to staff

loop.input: The approved protocol text for this skill.
loop.output: Teaching notes, each point tied to a protocol paragraph.
loop.check: Each teaching point quotes a paragraph of the approved protocol and adds no step that paragraph does not contain.
loop.stop: The acute care nurse accepts the notes or rewrites them after one draft.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed slide cannot follow a protocol paragraph that has just changed.

steps.what: Give informal education to other staff members
Lead the formal session with the same staff
Tick who attended that formal staff session

tasks.design: A draft in {DOCS} pulls teaching points from the approved protocol and cites the paragraph, and the acute care nurse checks that draft before using it. Giving informal education to other staff, and leading the formal session, stay in person at full time. The attendance tick stays with the nurse, and the session is not recorded.
tasks.previous_blocker: The teaching is a conversation at the bedside, and the protocol text changes in wording that a fixed handout misses.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can cite the current protocol paragraph. The nurse still checks it and still teaches.
tasks.still_hard: The informal coaching and the formal session, which depend on who is in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The nurse still decides what this colleague needs to hear and still runs the session.

ambition.what: Which protocol paragraph this session is allowed to teach, checked before every session rather than from memory.

tasks.altitude: The week is still teaching at the bedside and in the formal session. Less time goes to rewriting notes from a protocol the nurse already knows. The nurse still accepts the notes before teaching from them.

reach.task: Publish the protocol paragraph the teaching notes cite
reach.learn: Which paragraph the notes quoted, and which points the nurse rewrote.

evidence.claim: A draft that cites an approved protocol paragraph is a bounded read of that text. The nurse still teaches the session. This is model knowledge.
Providers are responsible for careful use of generative drafts, including knowing whether a tool is a medical device. The nurse accepts the notes before teaching from them.
Ambient recording that captures how staff perform needs works-council consent. This design does not record the teaching.

assumptions: The focal hour is preparing teaching notes, giving informal education, leading the formal session, and ticking attendance. Colleague time is not in this baseline.

Informal teaching and the formal session are in-person conversations the design does not change, so each stays at remaining 100. The attendance tick stays at remaining 100 because the nurse is the one who sees who was there.
The notes step shortens by half only because the draft quotes the approved protocol. The remaining half is the nurse checking those quotes.

The protocol fields are a document id, a paragraph id, and the paragraph text. The producer is the clinical educator, who already publishes the protocol. That writing is the educator's existing time, not this nurse's hour. If the protocol is missing, the nurse writes the notes and the draft saving does not apply.
Test the native document template before a custom screen.
The 2 incremental hours are refreshing the extract when the educator publishes a new paragraph, beyond the per-session check.
unknowns: Whether a current protocol exists for the skills this nurse teaches.
What share of the hour is informal bedside coaching rather than a booked session.
research_questions: What share of staff education has an approved protocol paragraph to cite?

already_counted.description: Checking the drafted teaching notes against the protocol paragraph stays in the prep step.
Informal education of other staff stays a full conversation.
Leading the formal session stays in full.
Ticking attendance stays with the nurse.

incremental.description: Refresh teaching extracts when the clinical educator publishes a new protocol paragraph.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Informal teaching (58), the formal session (16) and the attendance tick (8) stay at full time because the design does not change those steps. Only the notes (18) shorten, and only by half, because a draft quotes the protocol paragraph the clinical educator already published and the nurse still checks it. Gross 9 minus 2 hours of extract upkeep is a net of 7. The high end, 4, is a week where most sessions have a current protocol. The low end, 1, is a week of bedside coaching with no protocol, so the nurse writes the notes and that capture is not removed. The teaching itself is not claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collaborate with patients to plan future care and coordinate transitions and referrals.

steps.what: Read the record before the future health needs talk

loop.input: The problem list, the open referrals, and the free-text plan line.
loop.output: A short brief of what is already arranged for this patient.
loop.check: Every item in the brief appears in the record, and the brief adds no referral that is not written there.
loop.stop: The acute care nurse accepts the brief or discards it after one pass.
loop.why_not_simpler: A field copy cannot read the free-text plan line.

steps.what: Collaborate with patients on those future health needs
Coordinate transitions and referrals after the talk
Send the accepted referral for that transition
Tell the ward the agreed transition plan

tasks.design: A brief on {OTHER} shows the problem list and open referrals already stored, plus a bounded read of the free-text plan line, and the acute care nurse checks it before the talk. The talk with the patient, and telling the ward, stay in person at full time. The referral copies the identifiers and the destination the admissions clerk already stored, the nurse writes the clinical reason, and only that accepted version is sent.
tasks.previous_blocker: The plan lives in a conversation, and the referral was retyped from memory into a mail because the destination was not a field.
tasks.enabler_now: Stored problems and a destination id can fill the form. The nurse still writes the reason and still talks with the patient.
tasks.still_hard: The conversation about what the patient wants, and any transition with no stored destination.
tasks.human_edge: The nurse still agrees the plan with the patient and still writes why this referral is needed.

ambition.what: Whether the open referrals already cover the agreed need, checked before the form is sent.

tasks.altitude: The week still includes the talk with the patient and the handover to the ward. Less time goes to hunting the chart and retyping identifiers. The nurse still accepts every referral before it is sent.

reach.task: Store the destination service id before the nurse sends the referral
reach.learn: Which destination ids the referral form can copy, and which talks had none.

evidence.claim: Copying stored identifiers into a referral form is a field copy. The clinical reason stays with the nurse. This is model knowledge.
Annex III covers public eligibility for care and emergency triage. This brief is neither, and the nurse still agrees the transition with the patient.
The dossier is kept twenty years after the last change. The accepted referral is written into that dossier.
Health data are special category, and a solely automated decision about a person needs a legal basis. The nurse accepts the referral before it is sent.
Ambient recording of a conversation captures staff and needs works-council consent. This design does not record the talk.

assumptions: The focal hour is reading the record, the talk with the patient, writing the referral, sending it, and telling the ward. Patient time is not in this baseline.
The talk with the patient and telling the ward are in-person steps the design does not change, so each stays at remaining 100. The talk is not recorded.

The read step shortens by half only because the brief shows the stored problem list and open referrals and a checked read of the free-text plan line. The remaining half is the nurse checking the brief against the record.

Problem-list fields are a problem id and a status. Open-referral fields are a referral id, a destination service id, and a status. The producer is the clinician who wrote the problem and the admissions clerk who stored the destination. That entry is their existing time, not this nurse's hour. If those fields are empty, the nurse reads the notes and the brief saving does not apply.

The form step shortens by half only because identifiers and the destination service id are copied. The nurse still writes the clinical reason. If no destination id is stored, the nurse writes the whole form and that shortening does not apply.

The send is zero only for the version the nurse already accepted, and only when the destination id has an endpoint the admissions clerk stored. If the endpoint is missing, the nurse sends the message as today and the send saving does not apply.
The dossier entry stores the accepted referral text and a version id. It does not store a recording.
Test the native referral form before a custom screen.
The 2 incremental hours are directory corrections and referral reasons the receiving unit sends back.
unknowns: Whether destination services are already stored as ids.
Whether the plan line is a structured field or only free text.
research_questions: What share of transitions already has a destination service id before the nurse writes the referral?

already_counted.description: Checking the care brief against the record stays in the read step.
The talk with the patient about future needs stays in full.
Writing the clinical reason on the referral stays in the form step.
Telling the ward the transition plan stays in full.

incremental.description: Correct destination ids that fail, and rewrite referral reasons the receiving unit sends back.

approvals.approved_version: referral version the acute care nurse accepted

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The talk with the patient (46) and telling the ward (10) stay at full time because the design does not change those conversations. The chart read (18) drops by half only when the problem list and open referrals are already stored and the nurse still checks the brief. The form (14) drops by half only when the admissions clerk has stored the destination id; the nurse still writes the reason. The send (12) goes only for that accepted version, and only when an endpoint exists. Gross 28 minus 2 hours of corrections is a net of 26. The high end, 10, is a day when most patients already have a destination id. The low end, 2, is a day of free-text plans and no destination id, so the nurse still reads and writes and that capture is not removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Analyze indications, contraindications, and tradeoffs of therapeutic interventions.

steps.what: Gather indications and contraindications for therapeutic interventions

loop.input: The stored medication list and any free-text indication.
loop.output: Flags for interactions, contraindications, dose and duplicates, plus the indication words.
loop.check: Each flag names the rule and the two drugs, and the extracted indication uses the words written in the note.
loop.stop: The acute care nurse confirms the indication or types it, and stops after one pass.
loop.why_not_simpler: A code table cannot read a free-text indication.

steps.what: Analyze complications and the benefit tradeoffs
Tell the treating practitioner which intervention was chosen
File the accepted analysis of that intervention

tasks.design: The {OTHER} medication list, as ordered by the prescribing practitioner, is checked for interactions and contraindications, and the acute care nurse confirms any free-text indication. Analyzing complications and the benefit tradeoff stays a judgement at full time, as does telling the treating practitioner. The note files only the analysis the nurse already accepted. No price is invented.
tasks.previous_blocker: Indications were free text, and a missed interaction was a harm, so the nurse hunted the chart before every judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: An existing interaction check can flag coded drugs. The nurse still confirms the indication and still judges the tradeoff.
tasks.still_hard: The tradeoff for this patient, and any list that is not coded.
tasks.human_edge: The nurse still judges whether the benefit outweighs the complication for this patient.

ambition.what: Which flagged interaction is relevant to this indication, confirmed before the tradeoff is judged.

tasks.altitude: The week is still judging interventions at the bedside and telling the treating practitioner. Less time goes to hunting interactions when the medication list is coded. The nurse still accepts the analysis before it is filed.

reach.task: Keep the medication list and the indication on the order
reach.learn: Which orders the interaction check could read, and which indications the nurse had to type.

evidence.claim: The G-Standaard checks interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates, and the KNMP sets that content. The nurse still judges the tradeoff.
A prescription comes from a named practitioner. The interaction flag does not prescribe.
Providers must assess generative tools, and the inspector names medication errors from wrong registration. The nurse confirms the indication before relying on a flag.
Health data are special category, and a solely automated care decision needs a legal basis. The nurse makes the tradeoff.
There is no stored price for the intervention in this task, so a cost figure is not calculated. The tradeoff stays a human judgement. This is model knowledge.

assumptions: The focal hour is gathering indications and contraindications, judging the tradeoff, telling the treating practitioner, and filing the note. Prescriber time is not in this baseline.
The tradeoff judgement and telling the treating practitioner are steps the design does not change, so each stays at remaining 100.

The gather step shortens by half only because coded drugs are checked for interactions, contraindications, dose and duplicates, and a bounded read lifts a free-text indication for the nurse to confirm. The remaining half is that confirmation.

Medication-list fields are a drug id, a dose, and a route. The producer is the prescribing practitioner, who already ordered them. That order is the prescriber's existing time, not this nurse's hour. If the list is uncoded, the nurse looks the drugs up and the flag saving does not apply.
The indication, when free text, is confirmed by the nurse in the gather step. A model is not the last source of the indication.
No price field is assumed. Cost-benefit stays inside the judgement and is not a separate calculation.
The zeroed filing stores the analysis the nurse already accepted, including the tradeoff sentence written in that judgement. It does not choose the intervention.
Test the existing interaction check before a custom screen.
The 2 incremental hours are confirming indications the check has not seen before, beyond the per-case review.
unknowns: Whether medication orders on this ward are coded or free text.
Whether a price for the intervention is stored anywhere the nurse can read.
research_questions: What share of medication orders carries a coded drug id and a readable indication?

already_counted.description: Confirming the indication and reading the flags stays in the gather step.
Judging complications and the benefit tradeoff stays in full.
Telling the treating practitioner stays in full.

incremental.description: Confirm new free-text indications the interaction check has not seen, beyond the per-case review.

approvals.approved_version: analysis version the acute care nurse accepted

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The tradeoff judgement (48) and telling the treating practitioner (18) stay at full time because the design does not change those steps. The gather (22) drops by half only when the prescribing practitioner has coded the medication list and the nurse still confirms a free-text indication. Filing (12) stores the analysis the nurse already accepted. No price is calculated. Gross 23 minus 2 hours of new indications is a net of 21. The high end, 8, is a shift where most lists are coded. The low end, 2, is a shift of free-text orders, so the nurse still looks them up and that capture is not removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Distinguish normal from abnormal age-related changes in acute and chronic illness.

steps.what: Look up normal age related physiological ranges
Distinguish between normal and abnormal developmental and behavioral changes
Judge those changes during acute critical and chronic illness
Write the abnormal finding on the illness note

tasks.design: An age-band row the protocol committee stored is shown on {OTHER} next to the patient's age and the latest vital, which shortens only the lookup. Distinguishing a developmental or behavioral change, and judging it in acute, critical, or chronic illness, stay at the bedside at full time. The nurse still writes the note.
tasks.previous_blocker: Normal ranges sat in a protocol document, and whether a change was illness or age was a bedside judgement nobody else could see.
tasks.enabler_now: A stored age-band row can sit next to the age and the latest vital. It does not decide if the change is abnormal.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing the change in this patient, and writing what it means.
tasks.human_edge: The nurse still distinguishes a normal age change from illness in this patient.
tasks.altitude: The week is still at the bedside distinguishing changes and writing the note. The lookup of a reference range is shorter when an age-band row exists. The nurse does not gain a new decision right. The judgement stays theirs.

reach.task: Store the age-band low and high for each measure
reach.learn: Which measures the nurse still had to look up because the table had no row.

evidence.claim: An age-band table shows a stored low and high for an age. It does not decide whether this patient's change is abnormal. This is model knowledge.
Providers must know whether a generative tool is a medical device and must assess the risks. This lookup shows a stored range and does not judge the patient.
Age and vitals are health data. The view reads values already in the record, and a person distinguishes the change.

assumptions: The focal hour is looking up a reference range, distinguishing the change at the bedside, judging it in the illness, and writing the note.
Distinguishing the change, judging it in acute, critical, or chronic illness, and writing the note are steps the design does not change, so each stays at remaining 100.
The lookup shortens by half only because an age-band row is shown next to the stored age and the latest vital. The remaining half is the nurse reading that row.

Age-band fields are a measure id, an age band, a low, and a high. The producer is the protocol owner, who already publishes the range. That writing is the owner's existing time, not this nurse's hour. If the table has no row, the nurse looks the range up in the text and the shortening does not apply.

Patient age is produced by admissions and already stored on the record. The latest vital is produced by whoever charted it. If the vital is not charted, the nurse still observes the patient in the bedside step, and the view does not replace that observation.
The view does not classify the patient as normal or abnormal.
Test the native protocol table before a custom screen.
The 1 incremental hour is adding a row when the protocol owner publishes a range the table does not hold, which the nurse then checks.
unknowns: Whether age-band reference ranges are already stored as rows.
Whether the latest vital is charted before the nurse makes this distinction.
research_questions: What share of the measures this nurse checks has an age-band row already stored?

already_counted.description: Reading the age-band row stays in the lookup.
Distinguishing developmental and behavioral changes stays a full bedside judgement.
Judging the change in the illness stays in full.
Writing the illness note stays in full.

incremental.description: Check an age-band row when the protocol owner publishes a range the table did not hold.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Distinguishing the change (55), judging it in the illness (15) and writing the note (10) stay at full time because the design does not change those steps. Only the lookup (20) drops by half, and only when the protocol owner has stored an age-band row the nurse still reads. Gross 10 minus 1 hour of new rows is a net of 9. The high end, 4, is a shift where most measures have a row. The low end, 1, is a shift with no row, so the nurse looks the range up in the text and that capture is not removed. The bedside distinction is not claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still bedside care, teaching, and judging interventions. Less time goes to hunting a protocol or retyping identifiers when those fields already exist. The acute care nurse still teaches, still talks with the patient, and still decides the tradeoff and whether a change is abnormal. A draft does not have the last word.
reach: Clinical educator: publish the protocol paragraph the teaching notes cite, before the session.
Admissions clerk: store the destination service id before the nurse sends a referral.
Prescribing practitioner: keep the medication list and the indication on the order so the interaction check has a source.
skills_to_grow: Check a teaching note against the protocol paragraph before the session.
Confirm a free-text indication before judging an interaction flag.
role.ambitious_version: Each referral leaves with the reason the nurse wrote, and each intervention check starts from the stored medication list rather than a hunt through the chart.
